parole.significato: tusk, fang (e.g. that of an elephant or a boar)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *ɨnćara, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *ońćarɜ (“tusk”). Doublet of acsarkodik.

parole.significato: door (portal of entry into a building or room)
parole.testo: From the obsolete ajt (“to form an opening”) + -ó (present participle suffix). From Proto-Ugric *ᴕjɜ- (“come off, get looser, get free”). Related to Northern Mansi ойматаӈкв (ojmataňkv, “to free oneself”), ойтуӈкв (ojtuňkv, “to unfasten, to untie”), ойялаӈкв (ojâlaňkv, “to escape, to run away”). Com

parole.significato: to get stuck/caught (in something: -n/-on/-en/-ön, into something: -ba/-be)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *ϑᴕkkɜ (“get stuck; get at, meet”) + -ad (frequentative verb-forming suffix). Related to Northern Khanty тӑхрәмты (tăhrəmty, “to get stuck”).
Uncertain. Perhaps from Proto-Ugric [Term?] + -r (obsolete frequentative suffix).

parole.significato: to hang (to cause something to be suspended, e.g. from a hook)
parole.testo: From the same Proto-Ugric root as akad + -aszt (causative suffix).

parole.significato: litter, bedding, bed of straw (for animals)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *alama (“padding in shoes (made of hay), bed of straw”).

From Proto-Ugric *arɜ (“maternal relative”, “mother’s (younger) brother”), related to Northern Khanty орты (orty, “husband's younger sister”), орсәх (orsəh, “sister's daughter”). The Proto-Ugric word is probably a Proto-Iranian borrowing, compare Avestan 𐬠𐬭𐬁𐬙𐬀𐬭 (brātar), Ossetian ӕрвадӕ (ærvadæ, “br

From Proto-Ugric *θarańa (“gold, copper”), earlier *sarańa, compare Komi-Zyrian зарни (zarńi, “gold”), Eastern Mansi тарань (taranʹ), Eastern Khanty лорня̆ (lornjă, “copper”), Erzya сырне (sïrne). The Ugric word is probably a borrowing of Iranian origin, compare Avestan 𐬰𐬀𐬭𐬀𐬦𐬀 (zarańa), Old Persian
From Proto-Ugric *ϑasɜ- (“to dry, dry up”) + -ik (verb-forming suffix). Related to Northern Mansi тōсуӈкв (tōsuňkv, “to dry up”) and Northern Khanty состы (sosty, “to dry up”).

parole.significato: germ (the small mass of cells from which a new organism develops; a seed, bud or spore)
parole.testo: Uncertain. Perhaps from Proto-Ugric *ćᴕ̈rɜ (“sprout, blastus, embryo”). If so, related to Northern Mansi щӣрка (śīrka, “sprout, shoot”).

parole.significato: to kiss (to touch with the lips)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *ćukkɜ- (“to kiss”) + -ol (frequentative suffix).

parole.significato: to throw, to cast (to cause an object to move rapidly through the air)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *tᴕmpɜ- (“to throw down, to strike (with a clapping sound)”).

parole.significato: hill, mound, hump (an elevated location smaller than a mountain)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *tᴕmpɜ (“something lofty; hill, island etc.”). Cognates include Northern Mansi тумп (tump, “island”).
From Proto-Ugric *empɜ (“dog”). Cognates include Southern Mansi ǟmp and Northern Mansi а̄мп (āmp, “dog”).

parole.significato: to train somebody (to actively help someone else train)
parole.testo: Of disputed origin. Either from Proto-Ugric *ättɜ- (“to harden, chill (steel)”) (compare Northern Khanty аттыԓыйты (attyłyjty), аттәты (attəty, “to temper steel”)) or a derivative of a variant of the verb önt.

parole.significato: the far side; the region beyond something (e.g., a forest or boundary)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *älə (“other side”). Preserved in place names such as Erdély (“Transylvania”, literally “beyond the forest”).

parole.significato: glue, fish glue, size (a hard gelatin made by boiling bones and hides, used in solution as an adhesive, a natural form…
parole.testo: Probably from Proto-Ugric *äďɜmɜ.

Uncertain, thought to come from *eperyə (-y- preserved in dialectal epërj, and in eperjes ‘strawberry patch’), from *eperɣə, from Proto-Ugric *äppärĕ-kə (“strawberry”), from Proto-Uralic *äppɜ-rɜ-kɜ. Cognates include Western Mansi ӓпрӓ (äprä) (Lower Lozva), [script needed] (ǟpėrėχ) (Pelym) and South

From Proto-Ugric *eskä-, from Proto-Uralic *ećɜ- (“to fall”). Related to Northern Mansi исуӈкве (isuňkve, “to go down, to come down, to land”), Eastern Khanty ӓсәԓта (äsəłta, “to let go, to allow”), Udmurt усьыны (uśyny, “to fall”), Komi-Permyak усьны (uśny, “to fall”) and Kamassian ӱзə (üzə, “to de

From Proto-Ugric *paĺɜ (“icecrust, frost; to freeze”). Cognates include Northern Mansi по̄люӈкве (pōlûňkve, “to freeze”). For earlier proposed cognates such as Finnish palaa (“to burn”), see fal (“to devour”).
From Proto-Ugric *påda, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *padɜ. Cognates include Finnish pato (“dam”).

From Proto-Ugric *palɣɜ (“village”). Cognates include Northern Mansi па̄выл (pāvyl) and Eastern Khanty пуӽәԓ (puḥəł). Relationship to the Finnish verbs palvella (“to serve”), palvoa (“to worship”) has also been proposed.

parole.significato: lid, cap, top (cover of a container)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *pentɜ-lɜ (“lid, cover”). See also fed (“to cover”) + -él (noun-forming suffix).

parole.significato: to unstitch, untack (to take out stitches from a fabric)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *päčɜ- (“to part, separate, work itself loose”) + -t (causative suffix). Related to Northern Mansi песталаӈкве (pestalaňkve), пестуӈкве (pestuňkve, “to untie, to unbind”).

parole.significato: black (absorbing all light and reflecting practically none)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *pᴕ̈kkɜ-ttɜ (“black”).
From Proto-Ugric *pekkɜ- (“to split, crack, tear”) + -ly. A possible front-vowel variant of Proto-Finno-Ugric *pakka- (“to tear, split, rend”). Compare Hungarian fakad and fakaszt.

parole.significato: to sharpen, to whet, to hone
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *pänV-, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *pänä- (“to whet”).

parole.significato: to hold (to keep in one’s hands)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *puŋɜ- (“to grasp, to catch”). Cognates include Northern Mansi пувуӈкве (puvuňkve).
Uncertain. Perhaps from Proto-Ugric *pᴕlɜ- (“to stream bubbling”) + -ik.
Probably from Proto-Ugric *puśɜ- (“rag; to dissolve, fray”) (perhaps from Proto-Finno-Ugric?) + -lik (“verb-forming suffix”).
First attested in c. 1395. Probably from Proto-Ugric *puśɜ- (“rag; to dissolve, fray”) (perhaps from Proto-Finno-Ugric?) + -t (causative suffix).

parole.significato: to tire, get tired (to become sleepy or weary)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *pᴕɣrɜ- or *pᴕrkɜ- (“to get tired”) + -ad (frequentative suffix).

parole.significato: to tire (to make sleepy or weary)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *pᴕγrɜ- or *pᴕrkɜ- (“to get tired”) + -aszt (causative verb-forming suffix).

parole.significato: to be cold, to feel cold, to feel chilly
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric or perhaps Proto-Uralic *pᴕtɜ (“crust of ice/snow; to freeze”) + -ik. Cognate with Northern Khanty потты (potty, “to freeze”).

parole.significato: brake (a mechanical device that inhibits motion by absorbing energy from a moving system)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *päkkɜ (“bridle, rein”).

parole.significato: to stab, to prod by stabbing, to poke
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *pulɜ- (“to put, stick, stab, thrust”)
From Proto-Ugric *pičɜ + -t (noun-forming suffix). Cognate with Northern Mansi посым (posym, “smoke”) and Northern Khanty пөсәӈ (pøsəṇ, “smoke”).
From Proto-Ugric *pimɜ (“grass”). Cognates include Northern Mansi пум (pum, “grass”).

parole.significato: to heat, get heated (to become warmer)
parole.testo: Intransitive counterpart of fűt. Older meaning: 'to dry out; to burn out'. From Proto-Ugric *pilɜ (“to burn, be on fire”). Related to Northern Mansi пе̄ламтаӈкв (pēlamtaňkv, “to set fire, to light, to kindle”).

parole.significato: to lace (to fasten a shoe with laces)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *pĭtä-, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *pitɜ- (“to bind, to fasten, to tie up”). Related to Eastern Mari пидаш (pidaš, “to tie, to bind, to knit”).

parole.significato: plane (a tool for smoothing wood by removing thin layers from the surface)
parole.testo: Uncertain. Perhaps from Proto-Ugric *jᴕrɜ (“iron scraper”). Related to Northern Mansi ёръюӈкв (jorʺûňkv, “to plane wood”).

parole.significato: root (underground part of a plant that anchors and supports the plant body)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *jᴕ̈kkɜ-rɜ (“root”).

parole.significato: hair (of the head, excluding facial hair)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *kajɜ (“hair”), from Proto-Uralic *kaje (“grass, stalk”).

parole.significato: to bend, lean (usually of a person, out of his or her own will)
parole.testo: First attested in 1372. From the same Proto-Ugric root as hajt (“to bend”) + -ol (frequentative suffix).
From Proto-Ugric *kajɜ- (“to bend, stoop”) + -t (causative suffix).
Of debated origin: # From Proto-Ugric *kujɜ- (*kajɜ-) (“to chase, hunt, stalk, shoot”) + -t (causative suffix). # From hajt (“to fold”).
Inherited from Proto-Ugric *kaďma. Cognates include Northern Mansi хӯльм (hūlʹm).

parole.significato: ash (human or animal remains after cremation)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *kaďma.

Probably a derivation, but the root word is disputed: # From Proto-Ugric *kᴕmɜ (“clump in a marsh”) + -t (noun-forming suffix). # Split from han (“marsh, swamp”) (a variant of hany (“marsh, swamp”)) + -t (noun-forming suffix).
From Proto-Ugric *karɜ (“woodpecker”). Cognates include Northern Mansi хо̄хра (hōhra) and Northern Khanty хоӈра (hoṇra).
From Proto-Ugric *kaćɜ- (“break up, crack up, rip, tear”) + -ad (instantaneous suffix).
From Proto-Ugric *kaćɜ- (“break up, crack up, rip, tear”) + -ogat (frequentative suffix).
From Proto-Ugric *kaćɜ- (“break up, crack up, rip, tear”) + -ít (causative suffix).

parole.significato: swan (any of various species of large, long-necked waterfowl, of genus Cygnus, most of which have white plumage)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *kottɜŋɜ (“swan”), from Proto-Turkic *kugu (“swan”). Cognates include Northern Mansi хотаӈ (hotaň) and Eastern Khanty ӄө̆тәӈ (ḳø̆təṇ). See kuğu.
From Proto-Ugric *kurɜ- (“to draw, tug, drag, carry”) + -d (frequentative suffix). Cognate with Northern Mansi хартуӈкве (hartuňkve, “to pull, to draw, to drag”).
Lexicalization of Proto-Ugric *kućɜ (“side, place or room beside something”) + -á (lative case suffix, it also contains the similar possessive suffix which blended into the lativus suffix).

From Proto-Ugric *säptɜ (“seven”), borrowed from an Indo-European language (Proto-Indo-European *septḿ̥); compare Sanskrit सप्त (saptá), Ancient Greek ἑπτά (heptá). Initial h- is by analogy with hat (“six”). Compare Northern Mansi са̄т (sāt, “seven”).

parole.significato: to put on weight, fatten, to become fatter
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *katɜ- (“to become fat”) + -ik.
From Proto-Ugric *kumtɜ. Related to Proto-Turkic *kunduŕ, see it for more.
From Proto-Ugric *kupɜ-tɜ- (“to tear, pull, draw”).

parole.significato: young (in the early part of life or growth)
parole.testo: i (“small, young”, dialectal, only in compound words such as ileány (“little girl”)) + fiú (“boy”). The first part of the compound is from Proto-Ugric *äjɜ (“little, small, young”).

parole.significato: to get somewhere (to a location or a situation), to arrive
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *juktɜ- (“to come”). Related to Northern Mansi ёхталаӈкв (johtalaňkv, “to come”).

parole.significato: good (good for something (can be used for) -ra/-re, good at something -ban/-ben, good for someone (positively affects)…
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *jomɜ ~ *jamɜ (“good”). Cognates include Northern Mansi ёмас (jomas, “good, right, nice”) and possibly also Erzya ён (jon, “good, right, nice”).

Uncertain, perhaps from Proto-Ugric *kᴕ̈ntɜ (“mood”) with Hungarian derivation. The difficulty is that the origin of the final v is unclear. For the change of the internal *nt to d compare fed and ideg. Cognates include Northern Mansi кант (kant).

parole.significato: come and go, get about (to transport oneself from place to place)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *kälä-, possibly derived from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kälä- (“to ford”). Akin to Northern Mansi ква̄луӈкве (kvāluňkve, “to rise”).
From Proto-Ugric *kᴕ̈ćɜ (kᴕ̈ćɜ-rɜ) (“bitter”) + -eg (frequentative suffix).
From Proto-Ugric *kᴕ̈ćɜ (“bitter”) + -ű (obsolete present-participle suffix).

parole.significato: to accompany (to go with or attend as a companion or associate; to keep company with; to go along with)
parole.testo: Probably from Proto-Ugric *kećɜ- (“to track, pursue”) + -r (obsolete frequentative suffix).

parole.significato: millet (any of a group of various types of grass or its grains used as food)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *kᴕ̈lɜ, *kᴕ̈lɜ-ćɜ, *kᴕ̈lɜćɜ (“millet”).
From Proto-Ugric *kᴕ̈nɜ (“light”) + -ű (“diminutive suffix”).
Probably from Proto-Ugric. Another source indicates Proto-Finno-Ugric *kitɜ (“middle, gap”). Related to Eastern Khanty кӱтәп (kütəp, “middle, center; waist”).

parole.significato: to fight (whether literally or figuratively; for something: -ért or against something: ellen; (optionally) with someone…
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric or perhaps from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kᴕ̈śɜ (“competition, game; to compete, play”) + -d (frequentative suffix).
Uncertain. Perhaps from Proto-Ugric *lᴕćɜ (“wide, broad, loose”) + -a (diminutive suffix).

parole.significato: cover, hideaway, ambush (the place where one is concealed, in wait to attack by surprise, or the act of concealing ones…
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Ugric *läćɜ (“hiding place; lurk”). Cognates include Southern Mansi [script needed] (lǟš-), Northern Mansi лāщуӈкв (lāśuňkv, “to ambush, to waylay, to lie in wait, to wait for something”).

parole.significato: to step (to move by setting one foot forward, backward or sideways)
parole.testo: Possibly from Proto-Ugric *läppɜ- (“to go in, to enter”).
From Proto-Ugric *luɣǝ, possibly from Proto-Tocharian *l(ə)wa (“prey, livestock”) (whence Tocharian B luwo (“animal”)). Compare Northern Mansi лув (luv) and Eastern Khanty ԓӑв (łăw).

parole.significato: Hungarian, Magyar (of, from, or relating to Hungary, its people or its language)
parole.testo: From Old Hungarian Mogyër/Mëgyër/Megerhttps://uesz.nytud.hu/index.html?uuid=c194957f-7c44-1014-a8d2-ae24c20aeb7e * The first element (mogy-) is likely from Proto-Ugric *mańćɜ (“man, person”), also found in the name of the Mansi (ма̄ньси (mānʹsi), маньсь (manʹsʹ)). This may be an Indo-Iranian borrowi
From Proto-Ugric *mᴕrɜ (“hollow of the hand, palm of the hand”) + -k (nominal suffix).

parole.significato: warm (having a temperature slightly higher than usual, but still pleasant)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *mälɜ (“warm, to become warm”) + -eg (nominal suffix). Cognates include Eastern Khanty мӓлəӈк (mäləṇk), Northern Khanty мєләк (mêlək), Southern Khanty мельәк (mjel’ək) and Northern Mansi ма̄лтып (māltyp). Adjective sense 6 is a semantic loan from German warm, first attested in 1908.

parole.significato: to dare (to have the courage to do something)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *märɜ- (“to believe, have faith in dare”).

parole.significato: to ladle, scoop (to get some liquid or grainy substance out of somewhere by turning in a bowl-shaped object and let it…
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *märɜ- (“to dive, plunge”).

parole.significato: to stand out, to project, to jut out (upwards or in some other direction)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *merɜ-, *märɜ- (“to press, push; become narrow, contract”) + -d (frequentative verb-forming suffix).
From the same Proto-Ugric *merɜ-, *märɜ- (“to press, push; become narrow, contract”) stem as mered and merev + -ő (present-participle suffix).
From Proto-Ugric *mańćɜ, *maćɜ (“tale; to tell (tale, story)”).

parole.significato: field (land area free of woodland, cities and towns; open country)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *mećɜ- (“to put on clothing, to don”) + -ő (present participle suffix).

parole.significato: to smile (at or about something -n/-on/-en/-ön) (to have a smile on one's face)
parole.testo: Uncertain. Perhaps from Proto-Ugric *mućɜ-, *muśɜ- (“to smile”) + -lyog (frequentative verb-forming suffix).

parole.significato: to immerse (in liquid), to douse, to dunk (used with -ba/-be)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *marɜ- (“to dive, plunge”) + -t (instantaneous or causative suffix).
Probably from Proto-Ugric *mɤ̈̄lɜ (“to fit”).
From Proto-Ugric *melɜ (“deep”). Cognates include Northern Mansi мил (mil). and Eastern Khanty мәԓ (məł, “deep”).
From Proto-Ugric *mᴕ̈ɣɜ- + -t (instantaneous suffix). Cognate with Northern Mansi мувиньтаӈкве (muvinʹtaňkve)
From Proto-Ugric *ńärɜ (“to tear, pull, draw”).

parole.significato: saddle (a seat for a rider placed on the back of a horse or other animal)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *närkɜ (“saddle”).
From Proto-Ugric *ńalɜ (“eight”). Compare Northern Mansi нёллов (njollov, “eight”).
A word with disputed origins: # From Proto-Ugric *ńolɜ- (“to press”). # From Proto-Finno-Ugric *ńȣmɜ- (“to press, compress, crush”).

parole.significato: Nyék (one of the seven Hungarian tribes before and during the conquest of the Carpathian Basin)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *näkɜ- (“tie, bind”) + -k (noun-forming suffix).

parole.significato: side (a bounding straight edge of a two-dimensional shape)
parole.testo: Possibly from Proto-Ugric *oŋtɜ (“side (part of body), rib”). Cognate with Northern Mansi оӈтил (oňtil, “rib”).

Of debated origin: # From Proto-Ugric *alɜ- (“to add/fasten to something, fit”) Related to Northern Mansi ōлтуӈкв (ōltuňkv, “to extend, to elongate”) and Northern Khanty оԓԓыйты (ołłyjty), оԓтты (ołtty), оԓтыԓыйты (ołtyłyjty, “to join, to fit together, to elongate”). # Native word from the archaic a

parole.significato: whip (a pliant, flexible instrument used to create a sharp "crack" sound for directing or herding animals)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *oćtɜrɜ (“sprout, shoot, twig; whip”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *HáštraH.
Uncertain. Perhaps from Proto-Ugric *rᴕ̈ŋkɜ- (“to stick”) + -ad (frequentative verb-forming suffix).

parole.significato: to stick, cling (to someone or something: -hoz/-hez/-höz)
parole.testo: Uncertain. Perhaps from Proto-Ugric *rᴕ̈ŋkɜ- (“to stick”), a possible root of ragad + -aszkodik (frequentative-reflexive verb-forming suffix).
Uncertain, perhaps from Proto-Ugric *rᴕ̈ŋkɜ- (“to stick”) + -aszt (causative suffix).
Probably a lexicalization of Proto-Ugric *raŋɜ (“surface”) + -a (lative case suffix).

From a root of uncertain origin, perhaps Proto-Ugric or Proto-Finno-Ugric + -g (nominal suffix). The sz must have been a frequentative suffix that became part of the word. Its meaning may have referred to the saman's trance. (In the 1830s, Gregor Dankovszky compared the term to Austrian and Zipser G
Uncertain. Perhaps from Proto-Ugric *rᴕ̈ŋkɜ- (“to kick, kick at”).
Uncertain. Perhaps from Proto-Ugric *čajɜ- (“to press, push”) + -t (causative verb-forming suffix) + -ó (participle suffix).

parole.significato: part, phase, stage, section (e.g. of a day or a year)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric or perhaps from Proto-Finno-Ugric.

parole.significato: cart, wagon (a four-wheeled cart for hauling loads, usually pulled by horses or oxen)
parole.testo: Of disputed origin. Either from a pre-conquest Iranian loanword, or from Proto-Ugric *säkɜrɜ. First attested in 1067.

parole.significato: to race (to move or drive at high speed)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *sᴕŋɜ- (“to spring, run, gallop”) + -l (verb-forming suffix) + -d (frequentative suffix).
From Proto-Ugric *sᴕrɜ (“shin”).
Probably from Proto-Ugric *silɜ- (“acquire, obtain”). Cognate with Northern Mansi сэ̄луӈкве (sè̄luňkve, “to earn”).
Probably from Proto-Ugric *säŋɜ (“light, clear”).
From Proto-Ugric *säkrɜ (“hair”).
From Proto-Ugric *čettɜ- (“to become dark”).

parole.significato: to sink into/down (to descend slowly into a soft material/object)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *čeppɜ- (“to sink in/into”) + -ed (frequentative-reflexive verb-forming suffix).
From Proto-Ugric *čittɜ- (“to roast, to bake, to shine”). First attested in 1343.
From Proto-Ugric *täŋɜ-tɜ (“quiver (on belt)”).

parole.significato: to view, to look at something
parole.testo: Likely from Proto-Ugric *täkkɜ- (“to look (at), observe”) + -int (instantaneous suffix). Cognate with Eastern Khanty тӓɣӛнтӓ (täɣjəntä, “to remember”).
From *tätwə, from Proto-Ugric *täjəktəm (cf. Northern Mansi та̄кум (tākum), Northern Khanty тевтәм (tjewtəm)), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *täje (“louse”). Cognates include Finnish täi.

parole.significato: secret (a piece of knowledge that is hidden and intended to be kept hidden)
parole.testo: Probably from Proto-Ugric *tajɜ-ttɜ- (“to hide, keep something secret”) + -k (noun-forming suffix). Related to Northern Mansi тӯйтуӈкв (tūjtuňkv, “to hide, to conceal”). In turn, the Proto-Ugric word may be an early borrowing from Proto-Indo-Iranian (compare Avestan 𐬙𐬁𐬌𐬌𐬎 (tāiiu, “thief”), Sanskrit
From Proto-Ugric. Compare Northern Mansi тулмантанут (tulmantanut, “thief”) and тулмантаӈкве (tulmantaňkve, “to steal”).
From Proto-Ugric *turɜ (“throat, neck”). Cognates include Northern Mansi тур (tur), Northern Khanty тур (tur).

parole.significato: dish, bowl (a vessel such as a plate for holding or serving food)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *talɜ (“bowl or dish made of wood”).

parole.significato: space (physical extent across two or three dimensions; area, volume)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *tärɜ (“(open) space, room”).
From Proto-Ugric *tepɜ- (“lose one's way, be wrong, err, make a mistake”) + -ed (frequentative suffix). Cognates include Northern Mansi типуӈкве (tipuňkve).
From Proto-Ugric *tepɜ- (“lose one's way, be wrong, err, make a mistake”) + -lyeg (frequentative verb-forming suffix).

parole.significato: to miss, to make a mistake
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *tepɜ- (“lose one's way, be wrong, err, make a mistake”) + -eszt (causative suffix).
From Proto-Ugric *tüγɜtɜ or *tüwɜtɜ (“fire”). Compare Western Mansi тавт (tavt), Northern Khanty тўт (tŭt), Eastern Khanty тӱӽәт (tüḥət). Replaces Proto-Uralic *tule.
Uncertain, perhaps from Proto-Ugric *aktɜ- (“vomiting; vomit”) + -ál (frequentative suffix).

parole.significato: kidney, (attributively) renal (an organ in the body that filters the blood, producing urine)
parole.testo: Uncertain. Perhaps from Proto-Ugric, akin to Proto-Mansi *wäćəɣ (“penis”); cf. Northern Mansi восиг (vosig).

From Proto-Ugric *waŋke- (“to strike, cut”) or perhaps from Proto-Finno-Ugric *waŋɜ (“to strike, cut”). Cognates include Udmurt вандыны (vandyny, “to cut, to stab”) and Komi-Permyak вундыны (vundyny, “to reap, to crop”).

parole.significato: to wait for someone or something (with -ra/-re)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *warɜ- (“to guard, wait”). Compare Northern Mansi ӯруӈкве (ūruňkve, “to wait, to guard”).
Unknown. A Finno-Ugric or Ugric explanation is less likely. The Uralonet entry is marked with a question mark. See Proto-Ugric *wäńćɜ. Cognate with Central Mansi ви́шкаръ (víškarʺ).
From Proto-Ugric *ćuŋkɜ-, *(ćuŋkɜ-rɜ-) (“shrink, shrivel (up)”) + -odik (reflexive suffix). Possible cognates include Northern Mansi сюӈкырлаӈкве (sûňkyrlaňkve).
From Proto-Ugric *ćuŋkɜ-, *(ćuŋkɜ-rɜ-) (“shrink, shrivel (up)”) + -ít (frequentative-causative suffix).

parole.significato: nook, corner, recess (a small corner or a hidden or secluded spot)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *suŋɜ (“corner, angle”).

Lexicalization of earlier ált + -l (ablative suffix). The original ált is from Proto-Ugric *ᴕltɜ (“across, over”) (compare Northern Mansi ӯлтта (ūltta, “across, over”), Eastern Khanty уԓты (ułty, “across, over”)), from *o (“that”) + [Term?] (ablative suffix) + [Term?] (locative suffix).
From Proto-Ugric *ϑarɜ (“temporary lake coming into being during flood”).
Uncertain. Perhaps from Proto-Ugric. Compare Northern Khanty ԓўӈк (łŭṇk, “wedge, nail”).
Probably from Proto-Ugric *elɜ (“edge”). Compare with Northern Mansi э̄лми (è̄lmi, “edge”).
Probably from Proto-Ugric *eŋkɜrɜ- (“to say magic words, swear”).

Of debated origin: # From Proto-Ugric *jᴕ̈tɜ (“section, part (of body), limb; joint”). # From Proto-Finno-Ugric *jäse (“body part, joint”) (compare e.g. Finnish jäsen), though the development *s > z would be irregular.

parole.significato: heifer (a cow that has not yet had a calf)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *iśɜ (“mother, female animal”) + -ő (diminutive suffix).
